ASAD-NOTES:20:80#n63/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:20:80#n63/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:20:80#n63/r1.claim: Asad directs readers to note 38 on 19:52 and to 2:63 and 2:83 for the covenant with the Israelites.
ASAD-NOTES:20:80#n63/r1.anchor: As regards God's "covenant" with the children of Israel, see 2:63 and 83

ELMALILI:20:77-89/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:20:77-89/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:20:77-89/r1.claim: Elmalılı renders the appointment as on Ṭūr’s right side and identifies manna and quail as kudret helvası and bıldırcın.
ELMALILI:20:77-89/r1.anchor: ve size Tûr’un sağ tarafına vaad verdik ve üzerinize kudret helvası ve bıldırcın indirdik

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:80/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:80/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:80/r1.claim: The Qur'an recalls Israel's special blessings, ingratitude, and covenant at Sinai in other places, including 2:57-63.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:80/r1.anchor: Cenâb-ı Allah’ın İsrâiloğulları’na verdiği özel nimetler, onların nankör tavırları ve Tûr’daki sözleşme Kur’an’ın değişik yerlerinde hatırlatılmıştır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:80/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:80/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:80/r2.claim: The passage tells everyone to enjoy God's gifts without excess, never despair of mercy despite grave ingratitude, and seek forgiveness.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:80/r2.anchor: bütün insanlara, ölçüyü kaçırmadan Allah’ın verdiği nimetlerden yararlanmaları, –yaptıkları nankörlük ne kadar büyük olursa olsun– Allah’ın rahmetinden ümit kesmemeleri gerektiği mesajı verilmekte ve herkes Allah’tan bağışlanma dileğinde bulunmaya çağırılmaktadır.

BURSEVI:v5p314#3/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p314#3/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p314#3/r1.claim: Moses' counsel did not move Pharaoh; his refusal and obstinacy led to drowning and destruction, so a rational person should heed an adviser.
BURSEVI:v5p314#3/r1.anchor: واعلم أن موسى نصح فرعون ولكن لم ينجعه الوعظ فلم يدر قدره ولم يقبل فوصل من طريق الرد والعناد إلى الغرق والهلاك

BURSEVI:v5p314#3/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p314#3/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p314#3/r2.claim: Ḥāfiẓ's poem says the speaker learned the worth of valued people only in old age and asks God to bless the sincere adviser.

BURSEVI:v5p314#3/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p314#3/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p314#3/r3.claim: The contrast with youth warns that many young people turn to entertainments and away from divine counsel; one guided by God returns to himself and prays for the adviser.
BURSEVI:v5p314#3/r3.anchor: وفيه إشارة إلى أن وقت الشباب ليس كوقت الكهولة ولذا ترى أكثر الشباب منكبين على سماع الملاهي معرضين عن الناصح الإلهي

BURSEVI:v5p314#3/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p314#3/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p314#3/r4.claim: A wayfarer needs a guide, spiritual struggle, and discipline; merely having a guide is useless unless one follows, as Pharaoh knew Moses' truth but refused his path.
BURSEVI:v5p314#3/r4.anchor: ولا بد للسالك من مرشد ومجاهدة ورياضة فإن مجرد وجود المرشد لا ينفعه ما دام لم يسترشد ألا ترى أن فرعون عرف حقية موسى

BURSEVI:v5p314#3/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p314#3/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p314#3/r5.claim: The proper sequence is belief, acknowledgment, and effort; a ship cannot move across dry land, and the soul inclines toward ease and idleness.
BURSEVI:v5p314#3/r5.anchor: وقد قال بعضهم : "إن السفينة لا تجري على اليبس" والنفس تجر إلى الدعة والبطالة

BURSEVI:v5p314#3/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p314#3/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p314#3/r6.claim: The command to go forth lightly or heavily means worship remains obligatory until certainty, in ease or reluctance, and striving continues until the Resurrection.
BURSEVI:v5p314#3/r6.anchor: فالعبادة لازمة إلى أن يأتي اليقين حال النشاط والكراهة والجهاد ماض إلى يوم القيامة

BURSEVI:v5p314#3/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p314#3/r7.speaker: المولى الجامي
BURSEVI:v5p314#3/r7.claim: Jāmī's poem asks the reader not to despair over a long night of separation because the morning of union will eventually dawn.
BURSEVI:v5p314#3/r7.anchor:
قال المولى الجامي قدس سره :
بى رنج كسى ون نبردره بسر كنج

BURSEVI:v5p314#3/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p314#3/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p314#3/r8.claim: After Pharaoh and his people drowned, God addressed the Israelites, saying He had rescued them from their enemy.
BURSEVI:v5p314#3/r8.anchor: يا بنى إسراءيل} أي : قلنا لهم بعد إغراق فرعون وقومه وإنجائهم منهم

BURSEVI:v5p314#3/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p314#3/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p314#3/r9.claim: The enemy was Pharaoh and his people, who killed Israelite sons, spared their women, and forced them into hard labor; ʿaduww can be singular or collective.
BURSEVI:v5p314#3/r9.anchor: فرعون وقومه حيث كانوا يذبحون أبناءكم ويستحيون نساءكم ويستخدمونكم في الأعمال الشاقة والعدو يجيىء في معنى الوحدة والجماعة

BURSEVI:v5p314#3/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p314#3/r10.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p314#3/r10.claim: The right side of the Mount is defined from the travelers' direction from Egypt to Syria, since a mountain has no intrinsic right or left; the accusative describes the construct.
BURSEVI:v5p314#3/r10.anchor: بالنصب على أنه صفة للمضاف أي : واعدناكم بوساطة نبيكم

BURSEVI:v5p314#3/r11.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p314#3/r11.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p314#3/r11.claim: The appointment was Moses' meeting with God and receipt of the Torah; it is attributed to Israel because it concerned them and its benefit reached them.
BURSEVI:v5p314#3/r11.anchor: أي : إتيان موسى للمناجاة وإنزال التوراة عليه ونسبة المواعدة إليهم

BURSEVI:v5p314#3/r12.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p314#3/r12.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p314#3/r12.claim: Manna is a sweet, dew-like substance falling on trees, identified with taranjabīn.
BURSEVI:v5p314#3/r12.anchor: المن} هو شيء كالطل فيه حلاوة يسقط على الشجر

BURSEVI:v5p314#3/r13.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p314#3/r13.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p314#3/r13.claim: Salwā is a quail-like bird; during the wilderness wandering manna fell like snow from dawn to sunrise, one ṣāʿ per person, while a south wind brought enough quail for each man.
BURSEVI:v5p314#3/r13.anchor: {والسلوى} طائر يقال له السماني كان ينزل عليهم المن وهم في التيه مثل الثلج

BURSEVI:v5p314#3/r14.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p314#3/r14.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p314#3/r14.claim: The forty-year wandering punished their refusal to enter the giants' city, like a caring parent disciplining a child without withholding kindness; they still received effortless provision.
BURSEVI:v5p314#3/r14.anchor: والتيه المفازة التي يتاه فيها وذلك حين أمروا بأن يدخلوا مدينة الجبارين فأبوا ذلك فعاقبهم الله بأن يتيهوا في الأرض أربعين سنة

IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p245/r2.author: Ibn Khālawayh (attr.)
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p245/r2.speaker: author
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p245/r2.claim: The readings use first-person singular tāʾ or royal-we alif and nūn for God's speech; Abū ʿAmr drops the alif in ووعدناكم.
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p245/r2.anchor: إلا ما قرأه أبو عمرو من طرح الألف في ووعدناكم فمن قرأه بالتاء فالحجة له أنه جعله من إخبار الله تعالى عن نفسه

IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p245/r3.author: Ibn Khālawayh (attr.)
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p245/r3.speaker: author
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p245/r3.claim: The royal-we form follows the language of majesty; the author compares it with the speaker's plural in قال رب ارجعون.
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p245/r3.anchor: وعلى هذه اللغة يتوجه قوله ﴿ قال رب ارجعون ﴾

QIRAAT-ER:20:80:3#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:20:80:3#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:20:80:3#1/r1.claim: The Hamza variant changes orthographic treatment of the hamza in Isrāʾīl without a stated semantic distinction.
QIRAAT-ER:20:80:3#1/r1.anchor: alternative hamza treatment in the ʾāʾīl sequence

QIRAAT-ER:20:80:5#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:20:80:5#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:20:80:5#1/r1.claim: The singular first-person verb replaces the plural of majesty, intensifying God's personal agency in delivering the Israelites.
QIRAAT-ER:20:80:5#1/r1.anchor: singular first-person replaces plural of majesty, intensifying divine personal agency

QIRAAT-ER:20:80:9#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:20:80:9#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:20:80:9#1/r1.claim: The singular first-person in the covenant verb parallels the variant in the deliverance verb, intensifying personal divine agency.
QIRAAT-ER:20:80:9#1/r1.anchor: singular first-person in covenant verb paralleling the anjaytukum variant

QIRAAT-ER:20:80:9#2/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:20:80:9#2/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:20:80:9#2/r1.claim: Form I waʿada presents the promise as unilateral, replacing Form III's mutual appointment and removing reciprocity.
QIRAAT-ER:20:80:9#2/r1.anchor: unilateral promise replaces mutual appointment, removing reciprocity

QASHANI:20:80-82/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:20:80-82/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:20:80-82/r1.claim: The right side of the Mount is the heart’s mountain, facing the Holy Spirit and serving as the locus of revelation, called the inner inspiration and heart.
QASHANI:20:80-82/r1.anchor: الذي يلي روح القدس وهو محل الوحي الذي يسمونه الروع والفؤاد

QASHANI:20:80-82/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:20:80-82/r2.speaker: author
QASHANI:20:80-82/r2.claim: What was sent down means spiritual states and experiential ways, together with manna-like knowledge and certainty-based gnosis.
QASHANI:20:80-82/r2.anchor: من الأحوال والمذاهب من الذوقيات وسلوى العلوم والمعارف من اليقينيات

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p363/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p363/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p363/r1.claim: The verse recalls blessings in order: deliverance from humiliation, taxation, and slaughter; the religious benefit of Sinai and revealed law; then the worldly gift of manna and quails. Removing harm is a greater blessing than worldly gain.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p363/r1.anchor: وبدأ بإزالة ما كانوا فيه من الضرر من الإذلال والخراج والذبح وهي آكد أن تكون مقدمة على المنفعة الدنيوية

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p363/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p363/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p363/r2.claim: The apparent addressees are the Israelites saved with Moses after Pharaoh drowned.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p363/r2.anchor: والظاهر أن الخطاب لمن نجا مع موسى بعد إغراق فرعون

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p363/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p363/r3.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p363/r3.claim: Another view takes the address as an aside to the Prophet’s contemporaries, rebuking them because their forebears failed to thank God patiently; “your fathers” is understood by ellipsis.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p363/r3.anchor: وقيل: لمعاصري الرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم اعتراضا في أثناء قصة موسى توبيخا لهم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p363/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p363/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p363/r4.claim: All are addressed by واعدناكم although Moses chose seventy to hear God’s speech, because their hearing benefited and reassured all Israel.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p363/r4.anchor: وخاطب الجميع بواعدناكم وإن كان الموعودون هم السبعين الذين اختارهم موسى

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p363/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p363/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p363/r5.claim: The discussion of the right side of Mount Ṭūr is treated in Sūrat Maryam, and manna and quails in Sūrat al-Baqara.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p363/r5.anchor: وتقدم الكلام في جانب الطور الأيمن في سورة مريم، وعلى وأنزلنا عليكم المن والسلوى في سورة البقرة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p363/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p363/r6.speaker: حمزة، الكسائي، طلحة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p363/r6.claim: These readers have قد أنجيتكم and واعدتكم with first-person singular tāʾ; the other Seven read with majestic nūn, while Ḥumayd reads نجيناكم with doubled jīm.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p363/r6.anchor: وقرأ حمزة والكسائي وطلحة: قد أنجيتكم وواعدتكم ما رزقتكم بتاء الضمير

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p363/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p363/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p363/r7.claim: The commentary points to Abū ʿAmr’s differing reading and to the parallel واعد in al-Baqara.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p363/r7.anchor: وتقدم خلاف أبي عمرو وفي واعد في البقرة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p363/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p363/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p363/r8.claim: الطيبات means what is both lawful and delicious.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p363/r8.anchor: والطيبات هنا الحلال اللذيذ لأنه جمع الوصفين

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p363/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p363/r9.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p363/r9.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī analyzes الأيمن as genitive by proximity, like جحر ضب خرب; Abū Ḥayyān rejects this as too rare to explain a reading, preferring “blessed” or “on the right” of one facing the mountain.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p363/r9.anchor: قال الزمخشري بالجر على الجوار نحو جحر ضب خرب انتهى. وهذا من الشذوذ والقلة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p363/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p363/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p363/r10.claim: Israel must not overstep with its provisions by denying them, letting enjoyment distract from gratitude, spending on sins, or withholding required dues.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p363/r10.anchor: وأن ينفقوها في المعاصي ويمنعوا الحقوق الواجبة عليهم فيها

QUSHAYRI:v2p267/r1.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p267/r1.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p267/r1.claim: Pharaoh claimed the parted sea proved his majesty and divinity, then entered with his army; when the last had entered and the first hoped to escape, the waves drowned them all.
QUSHAYRI:v2p267/r1.anchor: فقال : ( إنه بحشمتي انفلق ، فأنا ربكم الأعلى ! )

QUSHAYRI:v2p267/r2.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p267/r2.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p267/r2.claim: Pharaoh’s confession came only after despair and could not help him because he persisted until the decree of damnation overtook him.
QUSHAYRI:v2p267/r2.anchor: وآمن فرعون لما ظهر له اليأس

QUSHAYRI:v2p267/r3.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p267/r3.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p267/r3.claim: God recalls His blessings to Israel and commands obedience and gratitude, including for the manna, quail, and trials given to their ancestors.

ALUSI-FULL:v16p238#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p238#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p238#2/r1.claim: The address to the Israelites recounts God's words to them after their enemy was drowned and they saved, following many religious and worldly blessings rather than occurring immediately.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p238#2/r1.anchor: حكاية لما خاطبهم تعالى به بعد اغراق عدوهم وانجائهم منه لكن لا عقيب ذلك

ALUSI-FULL:v16p238#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p238#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p238#2/r2.claim: A reported alternative treats the verse as a fresh address to Israelites in Muhammad's time, extending ancestral favors to them; al-Alusi rejects this because “وما أعجلك” and the context make that impossible.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p238#2/r2.anchor: انشاء خطاب للذين كانوا منهم في عهد النبي

ALUSI-FULL:v16p238#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p238#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p238#2/r3.claim: He prefers the narration of God's earlier address, supplied with an implied “قلنا” coordinated with “أوحينا.”
ALUSI-FULL:v16p238#2/r3.anchor: فالوجه هو الحكاية بتقدير قلنا عطفا على اوحينا

ALUSI-FULL:v16p238#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p238#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p238#2/r4.claim: The rescued enemy is Pharaoh and his people, who subjected Israel to severe torment by killing sons and sparing women.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p238#2/r4.anchor: فرعون وقومه حيث كانوا يسومونكم سوء العذاب يذبحون ابناءكم ويستحيون نساءكم

ALUSI-FULL:v16p238#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p238#2/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p238#2/r5.claim: Ḥumayd reads “نجيناكم,” doubled jīm with no hamza and a majestic plural; Ḥamza, al-Kisāʾī, al-Aʿmash, and Ṭalḥa read “أنجيتكم,” singular first person.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p238#2/r5.anchor: وقرأ حميد نجيناكم بتشديد الجيم من غير همزة قبلها وبنون العظمة وقرأ حمزة والكسائي والأعمش وطلحة انجيتكم

ALUSI-FULL:v16p238#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p238#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p238#2/r6.claim: For “جانب الطور الأيمن,” al-Zamakhsharī explains the genitive reading by attraction; Abū Ḥayyān says that is too rare and takes it as an adjective meaning blessed or to the right of someone approaching the mountain.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p238#2/r6.anchor: وقرئ بالجر وخرجه الزمخشري على الجوار نحو هذا جحر ضب خرب وتعقبه أبو حيان بأن الجر المذكور من الشذوذ

ALUSI-FULL:v16p238#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p238#2/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p238#2/r7.claim: Al-Alusi says rarity does not prevent the attraction analysis for a noncanonical reading; he rejects “right of whoever faces the mountain” and says it should mean right of one traveling from Egypt toward Syria.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p238#2/r7.anchor: والحق أن القلة لم تصل إلى حد منع تخريج القراءة لا سيما إذا كانت شاذة

ALUSI-FULL:v16p238#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p238#2/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p238#2/r8.claim: Some reject making “جانب” an adverb because it is bounded; Abū al-Baqāʾ instead treats it as an expanded object or supplies “coming to the side.” If adverbial, the promised event is Moses's meeting and receipt of the Torah there.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p238#2/r8.anchor: ونصب جانب على الظرفية ومنع بعضهم ذلك لأنه محدود وجعله منصوبا على أنه مفعول واعدنا على الأتساع

ALUSI-FULL:v16p238#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p238#2/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p238#2/r9.claim: The plural promise is attributed to Israel although only Moses was promised, because the event was connected to them and its benefit spread to them, heightening the blessing.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p238#2/r9.anchor: ونسبة المواعدة اليهم مع كونها لموسى عليه السلام نظرا إلى ملابستها إياهم وسراية منفعتها اليهم

ALUSI-FULL:v16p239/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p239/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p239/r1.claim: Ḥamza and the previously named readers read “واعدتكم” in the first person; another reading has “وَوعدناكم,” from the verb “promise.”
ALUSI-FULL:v16p239/r1.anchor: بتاء الضمير أيضا وقرئ ( ووعدناكم ) من الوعد

ALUSI-FULL:v16p239/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p239/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p239/r2.claim: The manna is identified as ترنجبين and the quail as السمانى; manna fell in the wilderness like snow from dawn to sunrise, a ṣāʿ for each person, while a south wind brought quail for them to take enough.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p239/r2.anchor: الترنجبين والسماني حيث كان ينزل عليهم المن وعم

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p287/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p287/r4.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p287/r4.claim: The rescued enemy is Pharaoh, and the Israelites are reminded of their appointment at the right side of the Mount and provision of manna and quail.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p287/r4.anchor: {يا بني إسرائيل قد أنجيناكم من عدوكم} فرعون، {وواعدناكم جانب الطور الأيمن ونزلنا عليكم المن والسلوى}

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p287/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p287/r5.speaker: حمزة، الكسائي
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p287/r5.claim: Hamza and al-Kisa'i read 'I saved you,' 'I promised you,' and 'I provided you' with singular first-person forms.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p287/r5.anchor: قرأ حمزة والكسائي: "أنجيتكم"، و"واعدتكم"، و"رزقتكم" بالتاء على التوحيد

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p287/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p287/r6.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p287/r6.claim: Other readers use the plural forms as an expression of majesty; all readers agree on the spelling of 'We sent down' with an alif.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p287/r6.anchor: وقرأ الآخرون بالنون والألف على التعظيم، ولم يختلفوا في {ونزلنا} لأنه مكتوب بالألف.

BAYDAWI-FULL:20:80-81/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:80-81/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:80-81/r1.claim: The address to the Children of Israel may follow their rescue from the sea and Pharaoh's destruction, with “We said” understood, or may address contemporaries of the Prophet by recalling what happened to their ancestors.
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:80-81/r1.anchor: بعد إنجائهم من البحر وإهلاك فرعون على إضمار قلنا

BAYDAWI-FULL:20:80-81/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:80-81/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:80-81/r2.claim: Their enemy was Pharaoh and his people.

BAYDAWI-FULL:20:80-81/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:80-81/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:80-81/r3.claim: The promised meeting at the right side of the Mount was with Moses, or with Moses and the seventy chosen men; it is attributed to the Israelites because of their association with them, for the meeting was to commune with God and receive the Torah.
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:80-81/r3.anchor: بمناجاة موسى وإنزال التوراة، وإنما عد المواعدة إليهم

BAYDAWI-FULL:20:80-81/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:80-81/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:80-81/r4.claim: The manna and quails were sent to them during the wilderness wandering.

BAYDAWI-FULL:20:80-81/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:80-81/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:80-81/r6.claim: Hamza and al-Kisaʾi read the rescue, promise, and provision verbs with first-person singular “I”; other readings include “I promised” and “We promised.”

BAYDAWI-FULL:20:80-81/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:80-81/r7.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:80-81/r7.claim: The genitive form of “right” follows “side” by proximity, like the expression “a lizard's stone, broken.”
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:80-81/r7.anchor: والأيمن بالجر على الجوار مثل: حجر ضب خرب

BIQAI-FULL:v5p33/r14.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p33/r14.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p33/r14.claim: God turns to Israel with reminders of past and coming favors, honoring them in light of their ancestry.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p33/r14.anchor: أقبلنا على بني إسرائيل ممتنين بما مضى وما يأتي

BIQAI-FULL:v5p33/r15.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p33/r15.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p33/r15.claim: God rescued Israel by His overwhelming power from an enemy who had regarded them as insignificant.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p33/r15.anchor: بقدرتنا الباهرة { من عدوكم } الذي كنتم أحقر شيء عنده

BIQAI-FULL:v5p33/r16.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p33/r16.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p33/r16.claim: God promised all Israel to appear in His presence and be honored at places of mercy; the Torah account is also mentioned in al-Baqara.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p33/r16.anchor: كما مضى في البقرة عن نص التوراة - للمثول بحضرتنا

BIQAI-FULL:v5p33/r17.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p33/r17.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p33/r17.claim: The right side of the mountain is on their right as they travel toward Abraham's homeland, facing the sea and the direction of Mecca and Yemen.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p33/r17.anchor: الذي على أيمانكم في توجهكم هذا

BIQAI-FULL:v5p33/r18.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p33/r18.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p33/r18.claim: The sequence first names a religious benefit and then worldly provision: the meeting and guidance precede manna and quails that sustain their bodies.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p33/r18.anchor: ولما بدأ بالمنفعة الدينية , ثنى بالمنفعة الدنيوية

BIQAI-FULL:v5p33/r19.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p33/r19.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p33/r19.claim: The manna and quails sustain Israel's bodies after the earlier rescue and promise of guidance.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p33/r19.anchor: بعد إنزال هذا الكتاب في هذه المواعدة لإنعاش أرواحكم

BIQAI-FULL:v5p35/r11.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p35/r11.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p35/r11.claim: The later apostasy contrasts with Israel's prior visible and audible signs, showing God's power to turn hearts contrary to expectation.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p35/r11.anchor: أتبع ذلك ذكر ضلالهم بعد رؤية ما يبعد معه كل البعد

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p274/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p274/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p274/r1.claim: Side of the mountain is in the locative case because its expanse makes it an indefinite place; the omitted object of the promise is intimate conversation.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p274/r1.anchor: وانتصب { جانب الطور } على الظرفية المكانية لأنه لاتساعه بمنزلة المكان المبهم . ومفعول المواعدة محذوف ، تقديره : المناجاة .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p274/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p274/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p274/r2.claim: The promise addressed to all Israelites was made to Moses and selected representatives, since the revelation of foundational law benefited the whole community.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p274/r2.anchor: وتعدية { واعدناكم } إلى ضمير جماعة بني إسرائيل وإن كانت مواعدة لموسى ومن معه الذين اختارهم من قومه باعتبار أن المقصد من المواعدة وحي أصول الشريعة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p274/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p274/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p274/r3.claim: The majority read the verb for sending down with the majestic plural; with the singular readings of Hamza, al-Kisa'i, and Khalaf for saving and promising, that plural is almost an iltifat, though technically not one.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p274/r3.anchor: فباعتبار قراءة حمزة ، والكسائي ، وخلف قد أنجيتكم وواعدتكم بتاء المفرد تكون قراءة وأنزلنا بنون العظمة قريبا من الالتفات وليس عينه ، لأن نون العظمة تساوي تاء المتكلم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p274/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p274/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p274/r4.claim: Manna and quails were discussed earlier in 2:57; the manna and quails episode occurred in the middle of the second month after leaving Egypt, according to Exodus 16.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p274/r4.anchor: والسلوى تقدم في سورة البقرة . وكان ذلك في نصف الشهر الثاني من خروجهم من مصر كما في الإصحاح 16 من سفر الخروج .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p274/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p274/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p274/r5.claim: Eat is omitted reported speech, estimated as We said or saying, as previously in the discussion of 2:57.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p274/r5.anchor: وجملة كلوا } مقول محذوف . تقديره : وقلنا أو قائلين . وتقدم نظيره في سورة البقرة .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p274/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p274/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p274/r6.claim: Most readers use the majestic plural in what We provided; Hamza, al-Kisa'i, and Khalaf read the singular form.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p274/r6.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور { ما رزقناكم بنون العظمة . وقرأه حمزة ، والكسائي ، وخلف ما رزقتكم بتاء المفرد .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p274/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p274/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p274/r7.claim: Tyranny concerning provision means neglecting gratitude for it and disregarding worship of the benefactor.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p274/r7.anchor: والطغيان : أشد الكبر . ومعنى النهي عن الطغيان في الرزق : النهي عن ترك الشكر عليه وقلة الاكتراث بعبادة المنعم .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p274/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p274/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p274/r8.claim: The preposition in in the provision phrase is metaphorical: tyranny is pictured as inhabiting an abundant blessing that surrounds its recipient like a vessel.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p274/r8.anchor: وحرف ( في ) الظرفية استعارة تبعية ؛ شبه ملابسة الطغيان للنعمة بحلول الطغيان فيها تشبيها للنعمة الكثيرة بالوعاء المحيط بالمنعم عليه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p274/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p274/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p274/r9.claim: The arrival of the effects of divine anger is pictured as an army settling in a people's land.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p274/r9.anchor: والحلول : النزول والإقامة بالمكان ؛ شبهت إصابة آثار الغضب إياهم بحلول الجيش ونحوه بديار قوم .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p274/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p274/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p274/r10.claim: Most readers use kasra in both forms of yaḥilla, deriving them from a debt coming due; al-Kisa'i uses damma, deriving them from settling somewhere, as the Kashshaf says without objection.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p274/r10.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور فيحل عليكم بكسر الحاء وقرأوا ومن يحلل عليه غضبي بكسر اللام الأولى على أنهما فعلا حل الدين يقال : حل الدين إذا آن أجل أدائه . وقرأه الكسائي بالضم في الفعلين

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p274/r11.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p274/r11.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p274/r11.claim: Ibn Malik and the commentator Bihraq al-Yamani omitted this distinction; al-Misbah's contrary claim is unreliable, while al-Qamus appears to allow the locative sense as transitive or intransitive, though Ibn Ashur found no supporting example.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p274/r11.anchor: وهذا مما أهمله ابن مالك في ( لامية الأفعال ) ، ولم يستدركه شارحها بحرق اليمني في ( الشرح الكبير ) . ووقع في ( المصباح ) ما يخالفه ولا يعول عليه . وظاهر ( القاموس ) أن حل بمعنى نزل يستعمل قاصرا ومتعديا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p55#3/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p55#3/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p55#3/r1.claim: The apparent reading addresses the Israelites at the time of these blessings, though time and events passed between the sea crossing and this speech and God selects what to mention.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p55#3/r1.anchor: ظاهر هذه الآية أن هذا القول قيل لبني إسرائيل حينئذ عند حلول هذه النعم التي عدد الله تعالى عليهم، وبين خروجهم من البحر وبين هذه المقالة مدة وحوادث

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p55#3/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p55#3/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p55#3/r2.claim: Alternatively, the address may target Muhammad’s contemporaries by recalling what God did for their ancestors; then eat is elliptical for it was said to them, and the passage rebukes their ancestors’ ingratitude. The author prefers the first reading as clearer.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p55#3/r2.anchor: ويحتمل أن تكون هذه المقالة خوطب بها معاصر ورسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم، المعنى هذا فعلنا بأسلافكم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p55#3/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p55#3/r3.speaker: ابن كثير ونافع وأبو عمرو وابن عامر
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p55#3/r3.claim: These readers have forms najjaynā, wāʿadnā, nazzalnā, and razaqnākum; Abū ʿAmr reads waʿadnākum without the alif throughout the Qurʾān.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p55#3/r3.anchor: وقرأ ابن كثير ونافع وأبو عمرو وابن عامر «نجينا وواعدنا ونزلنا ورزقناكم» إلا أن أبا عمرو قرأ «وعدناكم» بغير ألف في كل القرآن

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p55#3/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p55#3/r4.speaker: حمزة والكسائي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p55#3/r4.claim: Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī read anjait, wāʿadt, nazzalt, and razaqtukum.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p55#3/r4.anchor: وقرأ حمزة والكسائي «أنجيت وواعدت ونزلنا ورزقتكم»

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p55#3/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p55#3/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p55#3/r5.claim: Wāʿadnā may be a dialectal form of waʿada that does not imply two parties; if taken in its usual reciprocal sense, the Israelites’ readiness and resolve count as mutual appointment.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p55#3/r5.anchor: وقوله وواعدناكم قيل هي لغة في وعد لا تقتضي فعل اثنين ع وإن حملت على المعهود فلأن التلقي والعزم على ذلك كالمواعدة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p55#3/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p55#3/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p55#3/r6.claim: After saving Israel and drowning Pharaoh, God promised Moses and the Israelites they would reach Sinai so God could speak with Moses and give commands for their welfare.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p55#3/r6.anchor: أن الله تعالى لما أنجى بني إسرائيل وغرق فرعون وعد بني إسرائيل وموسى أن يصيروا إلى جانب طور سيناء ليكلم فيه موسى ويناجيه بما فيه صلاحهم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p55#3/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p55#3/r7.speaker: فرقة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p55#3/r7.claim: One group identifies this mountain as the one where Moses first heard God when he saw the fire on his way from Syria to Egypt.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p55#3/r7.anchor: وقالت فرقة هذا الطور هو الذي كلم فيه موسى أولا حيث رأى النار وكان في طريقه من الشام إلى مصر

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p55#3/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p55#3/r8.speaker: فرقة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p55#3/r8.claim: Another group says it is a different mountain.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p55#3/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p55#3/r9.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p55#3/r9.claim: Al-ṭūr is a mountain without grass; al-ayman can mean blessed or the right-hand side relative to a person or other reference point.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p55#3/r9.anchor: والطور الجبل الذي لا شعرا فيه وقوله الأيمن إما أن يريد اليمن وإما أن يريد اليمين بالإضافة إلى ذي يمين إنسان أو غيره

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p55#3/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p55#3/r10.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p55#3/r10.claim: Manna and quail were the Israelites’ food, whose interpretation was treated fully in al-Baqara.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p55#3/r10.anchor: والمن والسلوى طعامهم، وقد مضى في البقرة استيعاب تفسيرهما

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p311#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p311#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p311#2/r1.claim: The right side of the Mount is where the Torah was given; the author refers to his discussions of ‘right’ at 19:52 and manna and quails at 2:57.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p311#2/r1.anchor: واعدناكم جانب الطور الأيمن لأخذ التوارة وقد ذكرناه في مريم 52 معنى الأيمن وذكرناه في البقرة 57 المن والسلوى

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p308/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p308/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p308/r1.claim: God reminds the Israelites that He rescued them from Pharaoh, whom they watched drown with his entire army in one morning.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p308/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p308/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p308/r2.claim: Bukhari and Muslim report Ibn ʿAbbas saying that in Medina Jews fasted Ashura because God had given Moses victory over Pharaoh; the Prophet said Muslims had a greater claim to Moses and told them to fast it.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p308/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: لما قدم رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم المدينة واليهود تصوم عاشوراء

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p308/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p308/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p308/r3.claim: God appointed Moses and Israel at the mountain's right side, where He spoke to Moses, Moses asked to see Him, and He gave Moses the Torah; meanwhile the Israelites worshipped the calf.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p308/r3.anchor: وهو الذي كلمه تعالى عليه، وسأل فيه الرؤية، وأعطاه التوراة هناك.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p308/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p308/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p308/r4.claim: The manna was sweet food sent from heaven; quail were birds that fell to the Israelites, who took only enough for the next day, as mercy and kindness.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p308/r4.anchor: فالمن: حلوى كانت تنزل عليه من السماء. والسلوى: طائر يسقط عليهم، فيأخذون من كل، قدر الحاجة إلى الغد

NAHHAS:v3p52/r5.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p52/r5.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v3p52/r5.claim: Moses was told to bring the Israelites out with him so they could hear God speak in their presence.
NAHHAS:v3p52/r5.anchor: أي أمرنا موسى صلى الله عليه وسلم أن يأمركم بالخروج معه ليكلمه بحضرتكم فتسمعوا الكلام

NAHHAS:v3p52/r6.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p52/r6.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v3p52/r6.claim: The manna and quail were given to them in the wilderness.
NAHHAS:v3p52/r6.anchor: ونزلنا عليكم المن والسلوى ) أي في البرية

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p80/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p80/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p80/r1.claim: The address to the Children of Israel recalls their rescue from the sea and Pharaoh's destruction; although it may address Israelites in Muhammad's time, the author prefers the earlier audience.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p80/r1.anchor: خطاب لهم بعد إنجائهم من البحر وإهلاك آل فرعون ، وقيل : هو للذين كانوا منهم في عهد رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p80/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p80/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p80/r2.claim: The earlier address means “We said, O Children of Israel”; omission of “We said” is common in the Qur'an.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p80/r2.anchor: والوجه هو الأول ، أي : قلنا يا بني إسرائيل ، وحذف القول كثير في القرآن

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p80/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p80/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p80/r3.claim: A reading uses first-person forms from “We saved you” through “We provided you,” retaining the language of promise and covenant.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p80/r3.anchor: وقرىء ( أنجيتكم ) إلى ( رزقتكم ) ، وعلى لفظ الوعد والمواعدة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p80/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p80/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p80/r4.claim: A reading puts “the faith” in the genitive by attraction to a nearby word, like the phrase “a lizard's hole, broken.”
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p80/r4.anchor: وقرىء { الايمان } بالجر على الجوار ، نحو ( جحر ضب خرب )

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p80/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p80/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p80/r6.claim: The covenant is addressed to Israel because it concerned them through their prophet and leaders, and its benefits established their religion and law.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p80/r6.anchor: وإنما عدى المواعدة إليهم لأنها لابستهم واتصلت بهم حيث كانت لنبيهم ونقبائهم

MUQATIL:20:80-81/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:20:80-81/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:20:80-81/r1.claim: God rescued Israel from Pharaoh and his people and promised them the right side of the Mount, where Moses went with seventy men and received the Torah.
MUQATIL:20:80-81/r1.anchor: { يبني إسرائيل قد أنجيناكم من عدوكم } فرعون وقومه { وواعدناكم جانب الطور الأيمن }

MUQATIL:20:80-81/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:20:80-81/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:20:80-81/r2.claim: Manna in the wilderness was taranjabin appearing nightly on their trees, white like snow and sweet like honey.
MUQATIL:20:80-81/r2.anchor: أما المن فالترنجبين كان بين أعينهم بالليل على شجرهم أبيض كأنه الثلج، حلو مثل العسل،

MUQATIL:20:80-81/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:20:80-81/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:20:80-81/r3.claim: They gathered only enough manna for that day, except on Friday when they gathered two days' worth because they did no work on Saturday.
MUQATIL:20:80-81/r3.anchor: فيأخذون منه ما يكفيهم يومهم ذلك، ولا يرفعون منه لغد، ويأخذون يوم الجمعة ليومين،

MUQATIL:20:80-81/r4.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:20:80-81/r4.speaker: author
MUQATIL:20:80-81/r4.claim: Their garments grew along with their children, and men's clothes neither wore out, became shabby, nor grew dirty.
MUQATIL:20:80-81/r4.anchor: هذا لهم وهم فى التيه مع موسى، عليه السلام، وتنبت ثيابهم مع أولادهم، أما الرجال فكانت ثيابهم لا تبلى،

MUQATIL:20:80-81/r5.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:20:80-81/r5.speaker: author
MUQATIL:20:80-81/r5.claim: The quail was a bird sent after Israel asked Moses for meat in the wilderness and he asked God for it.
MUQATIL:20:80-81/r5.anchor: وأما السلوى وهو الطير، وذلك أن بنى إسرائيل سألوا موسى اللحم وهم فى التيه،

MUQATIL:20:80-81/r6.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:20:80-81/r6.speaker: author
MUQATIL:20:80-81/r6.claim: God sent a cloud that rained quail; the south wind gathered the red birds that traveled by Egypt, over an area a mile wide and to a spear's height.
MUQATIL:20:80-81/r6.anchor: فبعث الله سبحانه سحابا فأمطرت سمانا، وجمعتهم الريح الجنوب، وهى طير حمر تكون فى طريق مصر،

NASAFI-FULL:v3p63#3/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p63#3/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p63#3/r1.claim: The passage recalls God’s favor to Israel after He rescued them from the sea and destroyed Pharaoh and his people.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p63#3/r1.anchor: ثم ذكر منته على بني إسرائيل بعدما أنجاهم من البحر وأهلك فرعون وقومه

NASAFI-FULL:v3p63#3/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p63#3/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p63#3/r2.claim: The address to Israel reflects God’s order to Moses to travel by night with His servants and His words to the Israelites.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p63#3/r2.anchor: أي أوحينا إلى موسى أن أسر بعبادي وقلنا يا بني إسرائيل

NASAFI-FULL:v3p63#3/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p63#3/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p63#3/r3.claim: Their enemy is Pharaoh, and the appointment at the right side of the Mount was for the giving of scripture; God promised Moses this place and that he select seventy men to witness the Torah’s revelation.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p63#3/r3.anchor: وذلك أن الله عز وجل وعد موسى أن يأتي هذا لمكان ويختار

NASAFI-FULL:v3p63#3/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p63#3/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p63#3/r4.claim: The promise is attributed to Israel because it was made to their prophet and leaders and its benefits and law returned to them; al-ayman is accusative as an adjective of side.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p63#3/r4.anchor: وإنما نسب اليهم المواعدة لأنها كانت لنبيهم ونقبائهم واليهم رجعت منافعها التي قام بها شرعهم ودينهم والأيمن نصب لأنه صفة جانب

NASAFI-FULL:v3p63#3/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p63#3/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p63#3/r5.claim: A reading puts al-ayman in the genitive by attraction to the preceding word.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p63#3/r6.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p63#3/r6.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p63#3/r6.claim: Manna and quail were sent down to Israel in the wilderness.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p63#3/r6.anchor: ﴿ ونزلنا عليكم المن والسلوى ﴾ في التيه

QURTUBI-FULL:20:80-81/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:80-81/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:80-81/r1.claim: God reminds the Israelites of deliverance from Pharaoh so they will give thanks.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:80-81/r1.anchor: لما أنجاهم من فرعون قال لهم هذا ليشكروه.

QURTUBI-FULL:20:80-81/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:80-81/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:80-81/r2.claim: Grammatically, “the side” is the second object of “We promised”; it cannot be a bare locative because it is a definite place rather than an indefinite one.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:80-81/r2.anchor: «جانب» نصب على المفعول الثاني «لواعدنا» ولا يحسن أن ينتصب على الظرف لأنه ظرف مكان محض غير مبهم.

QURTUBI-FULL:20:80-81/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:80-81/r3.speaker: مكي
QURTUBI-FULL:20:80-81/r3.claim: Makki gives the implied wording as “We promised you arrival at the side of the mountain,” with the first noun omitted.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:80-81/r3.anchor: قال مكي: هذا أصل لا خلاف فيه وتقدير الآية: وواعدناكم إتيان جانب الطور ثم حذف المضاف.

QURTUBI-FULL:20:80-81/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:80-81/r4.speaker: النحاس
QURTUBI-FULL:20:80-81/r4.claim: Al-Nahhas says Moses was ordered to have the Israelites leave with him so God could speak in their presence and they could hear.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:80-81/r4.anchor: قال النحاس: أي أمرنا موسى أن يأمركم بالخروج معه ليكلمه بحضرتكم فتسمعوا الكلام.

QURTUBI-FULL:20:80-81/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:80-81/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:80-81/r5.claim: Another view says the promise was made to Moses after Pharaoh drowned: he would come to the right side of the mountain to receive the Torah, while the Israelites are addressed because the promise was for their sake.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:80-81/r5.anchor: وقيل: وعد موسى بعد إغراق فرعون أن يأتي جانب الطور الأيمن فيؤتيه التوراة

QURTUBI-FULL:20:80-81/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:80-81/r6.speaker: أبو عمرو
QURTUBI-FULL:20:80-81/r6.claim: Abu ʿAmr reads waʿadnākum without the alif; Abu ʿUbayd prefers it because the promise was God's to Moses alone, whereas mutual promising requires two parties.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:80-81/r6.anchor: وقرأ أبو عمرو «ووعدناكم» بغير ألف واختاره أبو عبيد لأن الوعد إنما هو من الله تعالى لموسى خاصة

QURTUBI-FULL:20:80-81/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:80-81/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:80-81/r7.claim: The mountain itself has no right or left; its right side is the side to Moses's right when he approached it.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:80-81/r7.anchor: و«الأيمن» نصب لأنه نعت للجانب وليس للجبل يمين ولا شمال، فإذا قيل: خذ عن يمين الجبل فمعناه خذ على يمينك

QURTUBI-FULL:20:80-81/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:80-81/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:80-81/r8.claim: Manna and quails were sent to the Israelites during the wandering in the wilderness; their explanation was given earlier.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:80-81/r8.anchor: { ونزلنا عليكم المن والسلوى } أي في التيه وقد تقدم القول فيه.

RAZI-FULL:v22p82#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p82#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p82#2/r1.claim: The account orders blessings by priority: rescue removes harm first, revelation is the greater religious benefit, manna and quails provide worldly benefit, then comes the ban on transgression and assurance that repentance is accepted.
RAZI-FULL:v22p82#2/r1.anchor: إزالة المضرة يجب أن تكون متقدمة على إيصال المنفعة ولا شك أن إيصال المنفعة الدينية أعظم في كونه نعمة من إيصال المنفعة الدنيوية

RAZI-FULL:v22p82#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p82#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p82#2/r2.claim: Rescue recalls Pharaoh’s many abuses of Israel, including killing, humiliation, expulsion, and exhausting forced labor.
RAZI-FULL:v22p82#2/r2.anchor: فإن فرعون كان ينزل بهم من أنواع الظلم كثيرا من القتل والإذلال والإخراج والإتعاب في الأعمال

RAZI-FULL:v22p82#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p82#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p82#2/r3.claim: The meeting at the mountain benefited Israel because God revealed a book explaining their religion and law; His speaking with Moses also brought them honor.
RAZI-FULL:v22p82#2/r3.anchor: ووجه المنفعة فيه أنه أنزل في ذلك الوقت عليهم كتابا فيه بيان دينهم وشرح شريعتهم

RAZI-FULL:v22p82#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p82#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p82#2/r4.claim: Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī read the rescue and promise verbs in the second person through the command to eat, except the manna clause, while the other readers use first-person plural throughout.
RAZI-FULL:v22p82#2/r4.anchor: قرأ حمزة والكسائي قد أنجيتكم ووعدتكم إلى قوله : { من طيبات ما رزقناكم } كلها بالتاء إلا قوله : { ونزلنا عليكم المن والسلوى } فإنها بالنون

RAZI-FULL:v22p82#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p82#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p82#2/r5.claim: Nāfiʿ and ʿĀṣim read wāʿadnākum, whereas Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī read wāʿadtukum.
RAZI-FULL:v22p82#2/r5.anchor: وقرأ نافع وعاصم وواعدناكم وقرأ حمزة والكسائي وواعدتكم

RAZI-FULL:v22p82#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p82#2/r6.speaker: الكلبي
RAZI-FULL:v22p82#2/r6.claim: Al-Kalbi says that after crossing the sea, Israel asked Moses for the promised book of duties and rulings; Moses affirmed and left for it, promising to return forty nights from his departure.
RAZI-FULL:v22p82#2/r6.anchor: قال الكلبي : لما جاوز موسى عليه السلام ببني إسرائيل البحر قالوا له : أليس وعدتنا أن تأتينا من ربنا بكتاب فيه الفرائض والأحكام

RAZI-FULL:v22p82#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p82#2/r7.speaker: الكلبي
RAZI-FULL:v22p82#2/r7.claim: Al-Kalbi explains the plural promise as God promising Moses the Torah on Israel’s behalf.
RAZI-FULL:v22p82#2/r7.anchor: وإنما قال : { وواعدناكم } لأنه إنما واعد موسى أن يؤتيه التوراة لأجلهم

RAZI-FULL:v22p82#2/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p82#2/r8.speaker: مقاتل
RAZI-FULL:v22p82#2/r8.claim: Muqatil explains the plural address as encompassing Moses and the seventy chosen men.
RAZI-FULL:v22p82#2/r8.anchor: وقال مقاتل : إنما قال : واعدناكم لأن الخطاب له وللسبعين المختارة

RAZI-FULL:v22p82#2/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p82#2/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p82#2/r9.claim: The mountain has no literal right or left; Sinai is called the right side because it lies to the right of a traveler from Egypt to Syria.
RAZI-FULL:v22p82#2/r9.anchor: ليس للجبل يمين ولا يسار بل المراد أن طور سيناء

RAZI-FULL:v22p82#2/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p82#2/r10.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p82#2/r10.claim: The reading al-ayman in the genitive follows its neighboring word, like the expression حجر ضب خرب.
RAZI-FULL:v22p82#2/r10.anchor: وقرىء الأيمن بالجر على الجوار نحو حجر ضب خرب

RAZI-FULL:v22p82#2/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p82#2/r11.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p82#2/r11.claim: The people benefited either from the Torah’s exposition of their religion or from the honor they gained when God spoke to Moses on the mountain.
RAZI-FULL:v22p82#2/r11.anchor: إما لأن الله تعالى لما كلم موسى على الطور حصل للقوم بسبب ذلك شرف عظيم

STUDYQURAN:20:80/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:20:80/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:20:80/r1.claim: The Israelites' rescue and manna and quails parallel other passages; the command to eat good provisions is also treated at 2:57.
STUDYQURAN:20:80/r1.anchor: For God’s sending down manna and quails to the Israelites and the command to eat of the good things We have provided you

STUDYQURAN:20:80/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:20:80/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:20:80/r3.claim: The Israelites later ask Moses for an idol like those worshipped by others and worship an idol while he is on Sinai.
STUDYQURAN:20:80/r3.anchor: For the Israelites’ asking Moses to make them an idol similar to the ones they found others worshipping

STUDYQURAN:20:80/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:20:80/r4.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:20:80/r4.claim: The appointed tryst on the Mount's right side refers to receiving the Torah, soon to be given to Moses at Sinai.
STUDYQURAN:20:80/r4.anchor: A tryst for the Israelites on the right side of the Mount refers to the reception of the Torah, which would soon be given to Moses at Mt. Sinai

STUDYQURAN:20:80/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:20:80/r5.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:20:80/r5.claim: The right side of the Mount is also associated with Horeb, where Moses met God and was chosen as messenger.
STUDYQURAN:20:80/r5.anchor: the right side of the Mount in reference to Mt. Horeb, where Moses met God and was chosen as a messenger

SAMIN-DURR:20:80/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:80/r1.speaker: الأخوان
SAMIN-DURR:20:80/r1.claim: They read أنجيتكم, واعدتكم, and رزقتكم in the first-person singular; the others use the majestic plural, and all agree on ونزلنا.
SAMIN-DURR:20:80/r1.anchor: قرأ الأخوان " قد أنجيتكم " و " واعدتكم " و { رزقتكم } بتاء المتكلم. والباقون " أنجيناكم " و " رزقناكم " و " واعدناكم " بنون العظمة.

SAMIN-DURR:20:80/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:80/r2.speaker: حميد
SAMIN-DURR:20:80/r2.claim: He reads نجيناكم with the intensive doubled consonant.

SAMIN-DURR:20:80/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:80/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:20:80/r3.claim: الأيمن is also read in the genitive; al-Zamakhsharī explains this as attraction to the preceding case, but the grammarian calls it odd and weak.
SAMIN-DURR:20:80/r3.anchor: وقرىء " الأيمن " بالجر. قال الزمخشري: " خفض على الجوار، كقولهم: " جحر ضب خرب " وجعله الشيخ شاذا ضعيفا.

SAMIN-DURR:20:80/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:80/r4.speaker: الشيخ
SAMIN-DURR:20:80/r4.claim: He instead makes الأيمن an adjective of الطور, either because the mountain is blessed or because it lies to the right of someone facing it.
SAMIN-DURR:20:80/r4.anchor: وخرجه على أنه نعت للطور قال: " وصف بذلك لما فيه من اليمن، أو لكونه على يمين من يستقبل الجبل ".

SAMIN-DURR:20:80/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:80/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:20:80/r5.claim: جانب is a second object with an omitted noun, understood as إتيان جانب; the second object cannot simply be omitted.
SAMIN-DURR:20:80/r5.anchor: و " جانب " مفعول ثان على حذف مضاف أي: إتيان جانب. ولا يجوز أن يكون المفعول الثاني محذوفا.

SAMIN-DURR:20:80/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:80/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:20:80/r6.claim: جانب may instead be an adverb of the promise: God promised the Torah at this specific place, since the verb does not directly take such a location.
SAMIN-DURR:20:80/r6.anchor: و " جانب " ظرف للوعد. والتقدير: وواعدناكم التوراة في هذا المكان؛ لأنه ظرف مكان مختص، لا يصل إليه الفعل بنفسه

SAMIN-DURR:20:80/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:80/r7.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:20:80/r7.claim: By extension, this place itself could be treated as the promised object, as Arabic says someone traveled two farsakhs or two postal stages.
SAMIN-DURR:20:80/r7.anchor: ولو قيل: إنه توسع في هذا الظرف فجعل مفعولا به أي: جعل نفس الموعود نحو: " سير عليه فرسخان وبريدان " لجاز.

TAB-FULL:v16p124#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p124#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v16p124#2/r1.claim: After Pharaoh's people drowned, God recalls the rescue of the Children of Israel from their enemy.
TAB-FULL:v16p124#2/r1.anchor: غشيهم، قلنا لقوم موسى: {يا بني إسرائيل قد أنجيناكم من عدوكم} [طه: 80] فرعون

TAB-FULL:v16p124#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p124#2/r2.speaker: قراء المدينة والبصرة
TAB-FULL:v16p124#2/r2.claim: Most Medinan and Basran readers use the first-person plural “We saved you,” as they do the other verbs in the passage.
TAB-FULL:v16p124#2/r2.anchor: فكانت عامة قراء المدينة والبصرة يقرءونه: {قد أنجيناكم} [طه: 80] بالنون والألف

TAB-FULL:v16p124#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p124#2/r3.speaker: قراء الكوفة
TAB-FULL:v16p124#2/r3.claim: Most Kufan readers instead use the first-person singular “I saved you,” but join the other readers in saying “We sent down.”
TAB-FULL:v16p124#2/r3.anchor: قرأ ذلك عامة قراء الكوفة: (قد أنجيتكم) بالتاء، وكذلك سائر الحروف الأخر، إلا قوله: {ونزلنا عليكم المن والسلوى} [طه: 80]

TAB-FULL:v16p124#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p124#2/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v16p124#2/r4.claim: Al-Tabari accepts both familiar readings because they agree in meaning.
TAB-FULL:v16p124#2/r4.anchor: أنهما قراءتان معروفتان باتفاق المعنى، فبأيتهما قرأ القارئ ذلك فمصيب

TABATABAI:20:80-82/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:80-82/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:80-82/r1.claim: This closing section of Moses' story counts God's favors to Israel, especially rescue, the Mount appointment, and manna and quail; it leads into the calf story and centers on Israel's exposure to God's anger.
TABATABAI:20:80-82/r1.anchor: يعد سبحانه فيه جملا من مننه على بني إسرائيل كإنجائهم من عدوهم ومواعدتهم جانب الطور الأيمن

TABATABAI:20:80-82/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:80-82/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:80-82/r2.claim: The address to Israel has an implied introductory We said, and their enemy is Pharaoh, whom God drowned after their long ordeal while saving them.
TABATABAI:20:80-82/r2.anchor: كأن الكلام بتقدير القول أي قلنا يا بني إسرائيل وقوله { قد أنجيناكم من عدوكم } المراد به فرعون

TABATABAI:20:80-82/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:80-82/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:80-82/r3.claim: The appointment at the right side of the Mount likely means Moses' forty-night appointment to receive the Torah; the stories of the manna and quail have also appeared in al-Baqara and elsewhere.
TABATABAI:20:80-82/r3.anchor: ولعل المراد بهذه المواعدة مواعدة موسى أربعين ليلة لإنزال التوراة وقد مرت القصة في سورة البقرة

TABATABAI:20:80-98#2/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:80-98#2/r3.speaker: القمي
TABATABAI:20:80-98#2/r3.claim: In the Qummi account, after Moses’s promised thirty-day absence passed without his return, the Israelites rebelled, threatened Aaron, and accused Moses of lying and fleeing.
TABATABAI:20:80-98#2/r3.anchor: فلما جاء الثلاثون يوما ولم يرجع موسى إليهم عصوا وأرادوا أن يقتلوا هارون وقالوا إن موسى كذب وهرب منا

TABRISI:20:80/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:80/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:20:80/r6.claim: Kufan readers except Asim use first-person singular forms for rescuing, promising, and providing; others use plural ن.
TABRISI:20:80/r6.anchor: قرأ أهل الكوفة غير عاصم قد أنجيتكم وواعدتكم ورزقتكم وقرأ الباقون قد أنجيناكم

TABRISI:20:80/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:80/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:20:80/r7.claim: Abu Jafar, Abu Amr, Yaqub, and Sahl read وعدناكم without alif; other readers read واعدناكم.
TABRISI:20:80/r7.anchor: قرأ أبو جعفر وأبو عمرو ويعقوب وسهل ووعدناكم بغير الألف والباقون بالألف

TABRISI:20:80/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:80/r8.speaker: أبو الحسن
TABRISI:20:80/r8.claim: He prefers وعدناكم because the alleged dialectal equivalence removes the implication of two agents that واعدناكم may carry.
TABRISI:20:80/r8.anchor: فاللفظ لا يدل على أن الفعل من اثنين فيكون القراءة بوعد أحسن

TABRISI:20:80/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:80/r9.speaker: author
TABRISI:20:80/r9.claim: Anjيناكم and واعدناكم are supported by the following plural verb نزلنا.
TABRISI:20:80/r9.anchor: فحجته قوله { ونزلنا عليكم المن والسلوى }

TABRISI:20:80#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:80#2/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:20:80#2/r4.claim: God rescued Israel from Pharaoh in their sight and promised Moses the Mount's right side after the drowning, where he would receive the Torah and its laws.
TABRISI:20:80#2/r4.anchor: وهو أن الله تعالى وعد موسى بعد أن أغرق فرعون

TABRISI:20:80#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:80#2/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:20:80#2/r5.claim: Manna and quails were sent during the wilderness wandering; their account appeared earlier in al-Baqara.
TABRISI:20:80#2/r5.anchor: يعني في التيه وقد مر بيان ذلك في سورة البقرة

THALABI:v6p256/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p256/r1.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p256/r1.claim: The delivered enemy is Pharaoh; God brought Israel to the right side of the Mount and sent down manna and quail.
THALABI:v6p256/r1.anchor: يا بني إسرائيل قد أنجيناكم من عدوكم فرعون وواعدناكم جانب الطور الأيمن وقد مر ذكره ونزلنا عليكم المن والسلوى.

THALABI:v6p256/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p256/r2.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p256/r2.claim: The general reading uses the plural first-person forms for God's majestic speech; Yahya ibn Waththab, al-Aʿmash, Hamza, and al-Kisa'i read singular forms.
THALABI:v6p256/r2.anchor: هذه قراءة العامة بالنون والألف على التعظيم، وقرأ يحيى بن وثاب والأعمش وحمزة والكسائي: أنجيتكم ووعدتكم ورزقتكم من غير ألف على التوحيد والتفريد

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p480#2/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p480#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p480#2/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says God recalls His favor to Israel: He rescued them from Pharaoh, whom He drowned before their eyes.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p480#2/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس: (ثم ذكر الله تعالى منته على بني إسرائيل فقال: {بني إسرائيل قد أنجيناكم من عدوكم} يعني فرعون أغرقه بمرآى منهم)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p480#2/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p480#2/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p480#2/r2.claim: After drowning Pharaoh, God promised Moses the right side of the Mount and would give him the Torah there, explaining what Israel needed; the author links this to 2:51.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p480#2/r2.anchor: وذلك أن الله تعالى وعد موسى بعد أن أغرق فرعون التأني جانب الطور الأيمن، فيؤتيه التوراة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p480#2/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p480#2/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p480#2/r3.claim: The verse has the readings wāʿadnā and waʿadnā.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p480#2/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p480#2/r4.speaker: الأخفش
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p480#2/r4.claim: Al-Akhfash treats wāʿadnā as a dialectal form of waʿadnā, so its alif does not prove reciprocal action, just as forms on the istafʿala pattern need not mean requesting an action.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p480#2/r4.anchor: وزعم أبو الحسن الأخفش أن: (واعدنا لغة في وعدنا)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p480#2/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p480#2/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p480#2/r5.claim: The author prefers waʿadnā because it plainly describes a promise by one agent; wāʿadnā is less explicit, so the clearer reading is preferable.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p480#2/r5.anchor: والقراءة بوعد أحسن؛ لأن واعد هاهنا بمعنى وعد، ويعلم من وعد أنه فعل واحد لا محالة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p480#2/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p480#2/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p480#2/r6.claim: Although the promise was made to Moses, Israel is addressed because the promise was for their sake.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p480#2/r6.anchor: وهذا الوعد إنما كان لموسى، ولكن خوطبوا به؛ لأن الوعد كان لأجلهم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p480#2/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p480#2/r7.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p480#2/r7.claim: The construction elides ‘coming to the side of the Mount’; the right side is the side to Moses’ right.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p480#2/r7.anchor: والمعنى: واعدناكم إتيان جانب الطور فحذف المضاف، والمراد بالأيمن الجانب الذي على يمين موسى

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p480#2/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p480#2/r8.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p480#2/r8.claim: An alternative interpretation says God promised Israel the mountain’s side so they could hear Him speak to Moses there.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p480#2/r8.anchor: وقيل في التفسير: (وعدهم الله جانب الجبل ليسمعوا كلام الله -عز وجل- لموسى بحضرتهم هناك)

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:77-80/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:77-80/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:77-80/r4.claim: God saved the Israelites from Pharaoh and promised them the Torah at the mountain's right side, where Moses would receive laws and rulings; Moses had promised them he would go there after leaving them.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:77-80/r4.anchor: لإيتاء الكتاب { جانب الطور الأيمن } وذلك أن الله سبحانه وعد موسى أن يأتي هذا المكان، فيؤتيه كتابا فيه الحلال والحرام والأحكام

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:77-80/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:77-80/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:77-80/r5.claim: Manna and quail were sent to the Israelites in the wilderness.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:77-80/r5.anchor: ونزلنا عليكم المن والسلوى } يعني: في التيه

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p269/r4.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p269/r4.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p269/r4.claim: God saved the Israelites from Pharaoh and his people.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p269/r4.anchor: قوله: {يا بني إسرائيل قد أنجيناكم من عدوكم} [طه: 80] من فرعون وقومه.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p269/r5.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p269/r5.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p269/r5.claim: The appointed right side is the right side of the mountain, and the appointment was with Moses.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p269/r5.anchor: {وواعدناكم جانب الطور الأيمن} [طه: 80] أيمن الجبل، والطور هو الجبل يعني مواعدته لموسى.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p269/r6.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p269/r6.speaker: قتادة
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p269/r6.claim: Qatada says manna descended at the Israelites' encampment like honey from dawn until sunrise.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p269/r6.anchor: سعيد، عن قتادة قال: المن كان ينزل عليهم في محلتهم مثل العسل، من طلوع الفجر إلى طلوع الشمس

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p269/r7.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p269/r7.speaker: قتادة، الحسن، الضحاك بن مزاحم
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p269/r7.claim: Qatada, al-Hasan, and al-Dahhak identify the quail as the bird called samani.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p269/r7.anchor: والسلوى هو الطير الذي يقال له السمانى. الحسن بن دينار، عن الحسن قال: السلوى السمانى. قرة بن خالد، عن الضحاك بن مزاحم قال: السلوى السمانى.

BURHAN:v3p171/r8.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p171/r8.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p171/r8.claim: ‘Wāʿada’ can take two objects while omitting one; ‘the right side of the Mount’ is the second object, not an adverb, with ‘coming to it’ or ‘staying there’ understood.
BURHAN:v3p171/r8.anchor: لا يكون ظرفا لاختصاصه والتقدير واعدناكم إتيانه أو مكثا فيه

BURHAN:v4p165/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p165/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p165/r1.claim: ‘Waʿada’ governs two objects and may omit one, like ‘give’ rather than ‘suppose’; ‘jānib’ is the second object, with arrival or stay implied.
BURHAN:v4p165/r1.anchor: فعل يتعدى لمفعوليين يجوز الاقتصار على احدهما كأعطيته وليس كظننت

BURHAN:v3p195/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p195/r4.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p195/r4.claim: In the command to eat manna and quail, an omitted ‘We said’ introduces the speech: ‘We said, eat,’ or ‘saying, eat.’

BURHAN:v3p212/r9.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p212/r9.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p212/r9.claim: The vocative particle is often omitted: 'you here,' 'Joseph,' and 'Lord' mean yā hāʾulāʾ, yā Yūsuf, and yā rabb; omission is common in possessive forms and divine address.

BURHAN:v1p288/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p288/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p288/r1.claim: Al-tur, the mountain, is listed as a Syriac word.

ITQAN:v2p320/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p320/r10.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p320/r10.claim: The salwa is a bird resembling quail.

IBNMUJAHID:v1p421/r9.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p421/r9.speaker: ابن كثير ونافع وأبو عمرو وابن عامر وعاصم
IBNMUJAHID:v1p421/r9.claim: These readers use three first-person plural forms with nūn and alif; Hamza and al-Kisāʾī use tāʾ without alif. Abu ʿAmr alone omits alif in وعدناكم throughout.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p421/r9.anchor: فقرأ ابن كثير ونافع وأبو عمرو وابن عامر وعاصم الثلاثة الأحرف بالنون والألف وقرأ حمزة والكسائى بالتاء بغير ألف

NASHR:v2p320/r12.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p320/r12.speaker: حمزة والكسائي وخلف
NASHR:v2p320/r12.claim: Hamza, al-Kisa'i, and Khalaf read the three verbs with singular first-person tāʾ and no alif—أنجيتكم, واعدتكم, رزقتكم—while the others use plural nūn forms with alif.
NASHR:v2p320/r12.anchor: أنجيناكم وواعدنا ورزقناكم فقرأ حمزة والكسائي وخلف

NASHR:v2p211#2/r3.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p211#2/r3.speaker: أبو جعفر والبصريان
NASHR:v2p211#2/r3.claim: Abu Jaʿfar and the Basrans shorten the alif, from simple promise; the others lengthen it, reading reciprocal appointment.
NASHR:v2p211#2/r3.anchor: فقرأ أبو جعفر، والبصريان بقصر الألف من الوعد، وقرأ الباقون بالمد من المواعدة
